messages:
pagerduty: P1 alert — elevated 5xx rate + latency spike in eu-west-1a. Affected: frontend fleet and ingress gateways. Trigger: network-path change / BGP flap detected. Link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/INC-1729987654 :rotating_light:

maria: acked. I'm the on-call. looking at metrics and routing now.

deepak: seeing BGP peer churn from ISP peer-8 for eu-west-1a, multiple withdrawn prefixes then re-advertise. traffic egress to core is intermittent, packet loss ~30-50% for a subset of hosts.

jess: app side — upstream connect_timeouts and a lot of retries. healthchecks to upstreams timing out, backlogs growing on edge nodes. draining not finishing on some nodes.

ops-bot: host-metrics gw-23a: egress-drops: 42%, net-errors spike at 1729987690. active connections falling to 20% of normal. attached logs: /var/log/gw/gw-23a/net.log (tail)

maria: quick sanity checks: dig on the service shows mixed IPs across regions (suspect stale routecache / DNS propagation issue).

```
$ dig +short service.frontend.prod.redwood
10.12.1.23
52.18.45.67
```

deepak: that second IP (52.18.45.67) is from eu-west-1b's LB, but routing is sending traffic from some AS paths through a peering we don't expect. suspect our routecache didn't invalidate after a prior traffic-shift.

jess: are we mid-traffic-shift or rollout? any recent canaries?

maria: there was a regional drain yesterday but no active shift scheduled. still investigating whether automated rollbacks or scheduled jobs touched routing.

alex: immediate mitigation plan: 1) abort any in-progress traffic-shifts; 2) force traffic to eu-west-1b for ingress (manual failover); 3) ask cloud ISP to investigate BGP anomalies. Maria, can you run rollback now? I'll coordinate comms. :eyes:

maria: running rollback command: `redwoodctl traffic rollback --region eu-west-1 --scope ingress --force` — starting now.

maria: executed rollback at 1729987730. pausing automated rollouts and removing eu-west-1a from LB rotation for the moment.

ops-bot: automation: traffic policy change detected by control-plane at 1729987735. policy-id: rp-9876.

deepak: also pushed ephemeral BGP reset to our edge routers in eu-west-1a to clear stale AS path. asked ISP to reset session.

jess: monitoring — 5xx count dropping from 80% -> 12% in the last 2m. upstream latency back to baseline for canary traffic.

ops-bot: alert update: majority of affected backends recovered. incident severity reduced.

ton y-csm: (cc) flagged for customer comms — a handful of customers in EU saw request failures for ~8 minutes. prepping a short status update to customers.

maria: handoff: @oncall-next — I'm handing off active monitoring and post-incident coordination. notes: root cause likely combination of ISP peering filter / BGP update + our routecache TTL not expiring quickly after a routing change. timeline and commands are in the incident timeline doc I just attached.

oncall-next: ack, taking over. I'll open an RCA ticket and schedule a 1-hour follow-up with net & infra. immediate remediation ideas: lower routecache TTL for regional egress entries, add automatic route invalidation on detected peering flaps, add canary traffic target to validate path before full shift.

alex: agree. add targeted synthetic checks from each az to verify egress ASN and path before we consider shifting 100%. also add a runbook step: on BGP flap, pause automated traffic-shift for 10 minutes.

maria: closing alert in PagerDuty, but keeping the Slack thread open for RCA notes. :white_check_mark: will create follow-up Jira: NET-2048 (routecache invalidation + runbook changes).

ops-bot: PagerDuty incident INC-1729987654 status: resolved at 1729987890.

ton y-csm: sent customer blast: "We experienced a brief regional networking incident in eu-west-1 that impacted ingress for some customers. Traffic has been routed to alternate AZs and we are monitoring. A follow-up with root cause and mitigations will be provided."

oncall-next: next steps doc created and assigned to deepak/jess/maria/alex. rough postmortem draft due EOD. I'll consolidate logs & BGP dumps.

maria: thanks everyone — great fast response. will include timeline and the commands we ran in the postmortem. handing off to oncall-next officially.

oncall-next: taking over monitoring for the next 2 hours, will escalate if anything regresses. :eyes:
